To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the proposed preprocessing strategy is able to reduce the number of concepts and their associations by 30-40%, (ii) semantic knowledge is able to enhance the quality and relevance of the discovered knowledge by up to 10%, and (iii) the best method for discovering knowledge from biomedical literature is our proposed method that combines the semantic knowledge with the null-invariant correlation measure Kulczynski.

1) the proposed methods are capable of discovering new knowledge, 2) the semantic knowledge is more useful than statistical information measures alone, and 3) the proposed preprocessing strategy helps in improving the overall performance of the system.
the combination of semantic knowledge with null-invariant information measures outperforms the traditional information measures in the context of biomedical knowledge discovery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a novel framework for discovering implicit facts and novel knowledge by integrating statistical information measures with semantic knowledge.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the semantic knowledge derived from domain ontology is a very important factor in determining the relevancy between terms and hence in discovering novel knowledge from the literature.
the proposed semantic knowledge-based information measures have outperformed all other information measures in the context of knowledge discovery.
the semantic knowledge, derived from domain ontology, is capable of improving the performance of the statistical methods, in terms of the precision and recall, by 10.4% and 11.2% respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, by incorporating domain knowledge, our proposed measures outperform traditional statistical measures.
the combination of semantic and statistical knowledge provides the best results.
the proposed methods can help in identifying novel knowledge from biomedical literature and can be applied in a wide spectrum of applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, the proposed methods are able to identify novel and potentially useful associations that may have otherwise remained unnoticed.
the proposed methods are able to discover new knowledge from the biomedical literature, which may lead to novel scientific hypotheses.
the use of semantic knowledge, which is derived from domain ontology, is a promising approach in the discovery of novel knowledge from large corpora.
